![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039918/assets/2102626f331aaa7803462f8e427ef2c0150deb554955199f3d402123934e815a.png)

A region is bounded by the curve $y={x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-1$ and $x=1$, as shown above. Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-2\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+3x){|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{4}-\frac{2}{3}+3)-(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{3}-3) \\  & =\frac{31}{12}-(-\frac{25}{12}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3} \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

A region in the $x$-$y$ plane is bounded by the curve $y={sec}^{2}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}$, and the $x$-axis between $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{3}$, as shown above. 
Find the area $A$ of the region. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}({sec}^{2}⁡(x)+\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sec}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)){|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{3})-(\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\sqrt{3}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}-\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡\frac{\pi /3}{\pi /6} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\end{aligned}
$$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=-{sec}^{2}⁡x$, the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$, as shown above. Find the area of the region.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}(-{sec}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{tan}⁡x{|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-(\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{tan}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =-(1-(-1)) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $2.$

Find the area between the curve $y=-{x}^{2}-1$, the $x$-axis, and the line $x=-1$ and $x=1$ (shown above). Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(-{x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{-1}^{1}-x{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =-(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3})-(1-(-1)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is 

$$
A=-{\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{8}{3}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}({x}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-4{\int }_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{-2}^{2}-4x{|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{{2}^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-2)^{3}}{3})-4(2+2) \\  & =-\frac{32}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\frac{32}{3}.$

$$

A region is bounded by the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and the $x$-axis between $x=-\pi $ and $x=0$, as shown above. What is the area of the region?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi }^{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x{|}_{-\pi }^{0} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )) \\  & =-1-(1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $2.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the area between the curve $y=x^2-2x+2,$ the $x$-axis, and the lines $x=0$ and $x=2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039918/assets/6b85f10cde49017eac1c56ad1b8abbcdf3033a367d5e1eb162dd89fbb6141461.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}-2x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{0}^{2}x\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{2}-2\cdot {\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2}+2x{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{8}{3}-0)-2(2-0)+2(2-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}-4+4 \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the area of the closed region between the curve $y=x^2-1$ and the $x$-axis.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the intersections of the curve with the $x$-axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-1 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =1 \\ x & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

We draw a sketch of the region, as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039918/assets/9b78aad41f84f6a6997914bd8d4243f30cb0ebea4edb5305962dc11c7a46a807.png)

We want the area between the curve $y=x^2-1$ and the $x$-axis, from $x=-1$ to $x=1.$ To find the area, we just need to compute the corresponding definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{a}^{b}y(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{-1}^{1}-x{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-(-\frac{1}{3}))-(1-(-1)) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}-2 \\  & =-\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we obtained a negative number. So the area that we want is $\dfrac{4}{3}.$
